o1.biggest_strength: It finds the top-5 matte stock-out and fixes it with re-cartoning, a rush order and a January trigger. The sums are right (25,000 x ₹207, total ₹1,14,13,400) and the glitter clearance steps avoid fake urgency.
o1.biggest_mistake: It leaves ₹5.87 lakh unspent and hedges with if/else rules on foundation shades and the January order, when the owner asked for one plan. It also looks over the 900-word limit.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut it to under 900 words, take out the conditionals so it reads as one decisive plan, and put the spare cash to work.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives one decisive plan: a rush and a standard order for the top 5 (₹1.187 crore total, all sums right), the re-carton job on Monday, and a dated action table. It shows stock at 6 Feb for every line and spells out the one-week gap honestly, with a back-in-stock line in the brand's voice and a nod to Tanvi's and Farah's words.
o2.biggest_mistake: The cap of 4 per shade works against Farah, who buys 6 to 10 units. The "any 2 for ₹999" liquid lipstick deal is roughly 29% off, even though the text says no deep discount.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Exempt pre-ordering artists from the cap, size the liquid lipstick offer to margin, and show the pre-order demand working.

reason: Both get the core call right: re-carton, rush the top 5, order nothing for slow lines, and stay inside ₹1.2 crore. Output 2 is tighter and more like one plan I can hand to my ops lead on Monday, with a dated action table, a cover forecast for every line and the cash put to work. Output 1 is a bit longer and hedgier.
